bottom_line: Global markets are reacting to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's return, driving a sharp rebound in US and Asian tech stocks.
Indian equities face a mixed setup, with a holiday yesterday and a significant banking sector decline on Monday.
Rising FPI inflows and strong PE/VC investments signal underlying confidence in India's long-term growth.

global.us: US stocks rebounded sharply on Monday, with the S&P 500 up 4.73% and Nasdaq Composite up 6.51%, driven by Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang's return. However, US futures are down today, with Nvidia giving back some gains.
global.europe: European markets are mixed to slightly down today, with the DAX falling 0.94% and FTSE 100 down 0.24%. Commercial real estate activity in the US fell 14% in October as interest rates rose.
global.asia: Asian stocks rallied significantly today, with the Nikkei 225 up 3.91%, KOSPI up 6.32%, and Taiwan TAIEX surging 8.99%, largely on the back of the Nvidia news and renewed AI trade optimism.

india: Indian markets were closed on Tuesday for Guru Nanak Jayanti. On Monday, the Nifty 50 fell 1.75% and the Bank Nifty dropped 3.17%, indicating a negative close before the holiday. FPI inflows reached ₹1 lakh crore in November, contributing to an 11% Sensex rally this month.
commodities: Brent crude is down 2.11% to USD 87.48, while WTI crude is up 0.82% to USD 80.83, with oil prices hovering near three-month lows on supply concerns. Gold and silver are down today, with gold at USD 3,614.50 and silver at USD 41.90, pressured by Fed rate hike expectations. Natural gas surged 13.72%. The rupee weakened against the dollar, trading at 92.90.

deep.title: Nvidia CEO's Return Ignites AI Stocks, Raises Governance Questions
deep.what: Nvidia's co-founder Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO, president, and board member after stepping down 11 days prior. This decision followed pressure from President Donald Trump and support from other tech leaders, triggering a 31.5% surge in Nvidia shares and adding over $1 trillion to its market value.
deep.why: Huang's return has revived the AI trade, leading to significant rallies in Asian and US tech stocks and boosting investor confidence in the sector. However, it also raises questions about corporate governance and the influence of political figures on board decisions, especially given the ongoing investigation into Nvidia.
deep.watch: Watch for further developments regarding Nvidia's internal investigation and any statements from the board or President Trump. Also, monitor the sustainability of the AI rally as US futures show some cooling.

deep.title: India's PE/VC Investments Surge to Five-Year High
deep.what: Private equity and venture capital investments in India reached USD 8.7 billion in October 2026, marking the highest monthly level in five years. This surge was primarily driven by eight large deals totaling USD 7.3 billion.
deep.why: This significant increase in PE/VC funding indicates strong investor confidence in India's growth potential and a robust deal-making environment. It suggests a healthy pipeline of capital for Indian companies, which can fuel expansion and innovation across various sectors.
deep.watch: Monitor subsequent monthly investment reports to see if this trend continues. Also, observe the sectors attracting the most capital, as this can signal emerging growth areas in the Indian economy.

deep.title: Government Plans IPO for India Infrastructure Finance Company Ltd (IIFCL)
deep.what: The Indian government plans to partially divest its stake in India Infrastructure Finance Company Ltd (IIFCL) through an initial public offering (IPO). The IPO is expected to include both a government stake sale and a fresh issue of shares by the company, targeting completion by the end of the current fiscal year.
deep.why: This IPO aims to monetize government assets and provide capital for IIFCL, a key player in infrastructure financing. It could attract investor interest in the infrastructure sector and provide a new avenue for public participation in India's growth story. The fresh issue of shares will also bolster IIFCL's capital base for future lending.
deep.watch: Monitor for further announcements regarding the IPO timeline, pricing, and the percentage of stake the government plans to divest. The success of this IPO could influence other government divestment plans.

deep.why: These potential tariffs could significantly impact Indian exporters, particularly in sectors targeted by the subsidies, leading to increased costs and reduced competitiveness in the US market. This could shift trade dynamics and potentially strain India-US trade relations.
